steps.name: Sample structure QC
caveats: Counts are salmon gene-level with unknown length correction: do not pre-scale; normalization happens inside the model in the DE step.
If a sample does not cluster with its expected condition cell, flag it and carry the flag into the DE step; do not silently drop the sample.
steps.context: Inputs: /eval-four-models-v2-with-interaction-2x2-n4-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (gene-level counts from salmon as delivered; profiled as 12000 rows x 17 columns, i.e. ~12,000 genes x 16 sample columns plus a gene column) and /eval-four-models-v2-with-interaction-2x2-n4-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (one row per sample with genotype, treatment, condition). First verify the sample columns of counts.csv match the sample IDs of metadata.csv 1:1 (expect 16 samples, 4 per cell) and report any mismatch before proceeding. Build the DESeq2 object directly from the delivered counts; the import state (length correction) is unknown, so use the counts as delivered without any pre-model scaling or normalization — size factors come from the model.
steps.question: Before any test, do the 16 brain bulk RNA-seq samples (genotype WT/KO x treatment vehicle/drug, 4 replicates per cell) form the expected 2x2 structure: do samples cluster by condition cell, are library sizes comparable across cells, and is any sample an outlier or mislabeled?

grounding.reason: Sample structure QC: vst(blind), PCA, sample distances per R-0033@40bf

constraints: Color the PCA and the distance heatmap by the condition cell, and separately by genotype and by treatment.
steps.description: Constructs the DESeq2 object from the delivered counts, verifies sample identity between counts and metadata, and produces blind-vst PCA and sample distance diagnostics for the 2x2 condition structure.
acceptance_criteria: DESeq2 object built from the delivered counts; sample names in counts.csv and metadata.csv verified 1:1, any mismatch reported.
PCA (blind vst, top 500 variable genes) colored by the four condition cells saved.

steps.name: DESeq2 2x2 factorial Wald test on the genotype:treatment interaction
caveats: Import state of the salmon counts is unknown (no per-sample quantification files, no average transcript length table delivered): fit the model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the outputs that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can appear as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table and do not invent a length input.

With 4 replicates per cell the interaction test is underpowered: the interaction coefficient is a difference of differences with a large standard error, so a non-significant interaction is not proof of no genotype-by-drug difference.
Do not test a fold-change threshold by post-hoc filtering; a threshold belongs inside the test (lfcThreshold).
steps.context: 2x2 factorial, 4 biological replicates per cell, ~12,000 genes. Design formula ~ genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment with explicit reference levels: relevel genotype so WT is the reference and relevel treatment so vehicle is the reference before building the design (never rely on alphabetical order, which would put KO and drug as references). Primary test: Wald test of the interaction coefficient (genotypeKO.treatmentdrug) per gene — this is the direct answer to the research question. Simple effects, reported per gene: (1) drug vs vehicle in WT = coefficient treatmentdrug; (2) drug vs vehicle in KO = contrast summing treatmentdrug + genotypeKO.treatmentdrug. Pre-filter before the model: keep genes with at least 10 counts in at least 4 samples (the smallest group size). Normalization is inside DESeq2 (median-of-ratios size factors); no pre-normalization. Keep DESeq2's default count-outlier behavior (with 4 replicates per cell, Cook's-distance outliers are flagged and that gene's p-values become NA). Multiple testing: Benjamini-Hochberg within each of the three contrasts at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering on, and the same alpha passed to results(); report the contrast name beside every adjusted p-value. Shrink the reported log2FC with ashr for the KO simple effect (a two-coefficient contrast; apeglm accepts a single coefficient only), and report unshrunken and shrunken values side by side. Inspect the unadjusted p-value histogram of each contrast before trusting the adjustment.
steps.question: Does the effect of drug vs vehicle on gene expression differ between KO and WT (the genotype:treatment interaction), and what are the simple effects of drug vs vehicle within WT and within KO?

grounding.reason: DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm/ashr log fold change shrinkage per R-0029@22ca and R-0001@9a17; interaction question per R-0013@2639; unknown salmon import state handled per R-0169@18ab (counts as delivered, no length offset).

steps.description: DESeq2 2x2 factorial model (genotype + treatment + interaction, reference levels WT and vehicle) with a Wald test of the interaction coefficient per gene, simple drug effects within each genotype, ashr-shrunken fold changes, BH multiple testing within each contrast, and p-value histogram diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria: Result tables for all three contrasts (genotype:treatment interaction; drug in WT; drug in KO), each with gene, unshrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, ashr-shrunken log2FoldChange, pvalue, padj.
Number of genes tested after the pre-filter reported; genes with NA padj from the Cook's-distance outlier flag reported separately from genes dropped by independent filtering.
Unadjusted p-value histogram per contrast saved and its shape assessed before the adjusted p-values are used.
Reference levels (genotype: WT; treatment: vehicle) and the design formula written into the outputs.

steps.name: Report
caveats: Never rank by the unshrunken log2FC alone; keep the p-values from the unshrunken fit.
Do not present a single significant simple effect as the answer to the interaction question — the interaction contrast is the answer.
steps.context: Assemble the final report from the T1S1 and T1S2 outputs. Per gene, present the three results side by side: the drug effect at the reference genotype (WT), the drug effect at the other genotype (KO), and the interaction contrast (difference of the two); name the reference level of each factor beside the table (genotype: WT; treatment: vehicle). The answer to the research question is the interaction contrast: report the number of interaction genes significant at padj < 0.05, and note that a significant interaction does not by itself say which genotype the drug affects (that comes from the simple effects), while a non-significant interaction is not proof of no difference given the limited power.
steps.question: What is the evidence-based answer to whether the drug acts differently in KO than in WT — the interaction result, the simple drug effects in each genotype, the fit diagnostics, and the limitations of the result?

grounding.reason: No rule covers this step; the robustness setting deviates from the skeleton (overlap_of_two_methods) because the knowledge check restricted the DE method in this situation to the DESeq2 Wald test, so a second method cannot be produced — the step states the deviation and its reason.

steps.description: Final report answering the interaction question: per-gene simple effects plus interaction contrast side by side, fit diagnostics, significance counts, and the explicit power and import-state limitations.
acceptance_criteria: Per-gene table with the three interaction-related results side by side (drug effect in WT, drug effect in KO, interaction contrast), reference levels named, ranked on the shrunken log2FC.
MA plot and dispersion plot present, each with a one-line reading of what it shows.
p-value histogram per contrast with its shape stated.

Report header names the method (DESeq2), package versions, design formula and reference levels, thresholds (padj < 0.05), number of genes tested, and number of DE genes per contrast; sessionInfo attached.

Explicit limitation statements: (a) length offset lost because the salmon counts are used as delivered; (b) interaction test power limited with 4 replicates per cell; (c) two-method robustness overlap not run because only the DESeq2 Wald test is permitted for this situation.

plan.title: 2x2 DE: does drug act differently in KO
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question is a genotype-by-treatment interaction in human brain bulk RNA-seq: 16 samples, 4 replicates per cell of a 2x2 design (genotype WT/KO x treatment vehicle/drug), ~12,000 genes, salmon gene-level counts. The import state of the counts is unknown (no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table were delivered), so per the procedure the model is fit on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and the report states that a change in isoform use can appear as differential expression. Sample structure QC (blind vst, PCA, distance heatmap) runs first to confirm the 2x2 grouping before any test. DESeq2 then fits ~ genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment with explicit reference levels (genotype: WT, treatment: vehicle) and tests the interaction coefficient per gene with the Wald test — the direct answer to whether the drug acts differently in KO than in WT — followed by the simple effects of drug vs vehicle within WT and within KO, ashr-shrunken fold changes for the multi-coefficient contrasts, Benjamini-Hochberg correction within each contrast at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering, and p-value histogram inspection before adjustment. The report presents the interaction contrast and both simple effects per gene side by side, with fit diagnostics and the power/import limitations stated.

DESeq2 Wald test on the interaction coefficient (primary), edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same design as second method for robustness
ashr log2 fold change shrinkage for multi-coefficient contrasts
Benjamini-Hochberg within each contrast with independent filtering

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

steps.method: DESeq2 vst (blind) + PCA on top variable genes + sample distance heatmap
minimal pre-filter plus independent filtering in results
median of ratios size factors inside DESeq2
two-factor factorial design with interaction, explicit reference levels (genotype: WT, treatment: vehicle)
DESeq2 Wald test on the interaction coefficient (primary), edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same design as second method for robustness
ashr log2 fold change shrinkage for multi-coefficient contrasts
Benjamini-Hochberg within each contrast with independent filtering

permitted: Low count filter: keep a gene with at least 10 counts in at least the smallest group size of samples
